title: The Time Flowing on the Canal
subtitle: A documentary project on the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal created by the Social Narrative Studio of the China Academy of Art

mainContent.content: A documentary and interactive experience design project treating the Grand Canal as living time. Visitors navigate a multi-sensory exhibition through physical models, projection mapping, and telescopic views.

content.title: Detailed diorama of the Grand Canal showing traditional buildings, bridges, and waterways in a dark wooden box

mainContent.content: A finely crafted diorama in a dark wooden box captures the canal's traditional architecture, bridges, and waterways in miniature.

content.title: Exhibition space with bamboo railings creating pathways, wall projections showing canal scenes

mainContent.content: Bamboo railings create guided pathways through the gallery. Wall projections immerse visitors in canal scenes at multiple scales.

content.title: View through a telescope/peephole showing historical canal scene with traditional architecture

mainContent.content: Looking through a telescope reveals a historical canal view — traditional buildings and boats along the waterway, creating an intimate micro-perspective.

content.title: Paper-cut art and geometric models displayed alongside project documentation

mainContent.content: Paper-cut installations and geometric models sit alongside project binders, showing the research and craft behind the narrative design.

Documentary research becomes immersive spatial narrative. Visitors move between macro and micro scales. Bamboo and wood evoke the canal's historical architecture, grounding narrative in tactile reality.
